summary: Implemented explicit link/reparse and special-file scope policy. Search now skips reparse points by default, follows supported targets only when requested with physical containment and visited-directory guards, preserves hard-linked path identity, and excludes special entries before content open.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search implementation and its tests were changed, together with W04-S04 evidence. No public SQL/source signature, sibling repository, query-engine adapter, release or publish surface was modified.

classification.reparse: Filesystem attributes and link-target metadata identify reparse entries before they are yielded. The default action and Search scope policy both refuse reparse entries unless FollowLinks is explicit.
classification.special: Entries reported with FileAttributes.Device are marked special and skipped before metadata or content access. No FIFO/socket/device-reading mode is exposed.
classification.broken: Broken or unsupported link targets are skipped as non-regular candidates.
classification.root: The scope matcher prepares an explicit root before traversal, so a reparse file or directory root cannot bypass the default no-follow policy.
classification.hardLinks: Hard-linked files remain separate lexical path candidates; no file-ID deduplication changes Search path evidence.

followPolicy.containment: Resolved link targets must remain under the resolved physical root before convenience filters or content reads are reached.
followPolicy.cycles: Resolution is bounded and tracks link paths; traversal tracks normalized physical directory identities, stopping ancestor cycles and duplicate directory aliases.
followPolicy.cancellation: A cancellation check runs between link-resolution steps, while the existing traversal frontier and reader disposal remain in force.
followPolicy.outsideRoot: A followed descendant link whose resolved target is outside the physical root raises the established typed SEARCH-SOURCE-002 source-access diagnostic at the link path.

implementation.publicBinding: The existing FollowLinks policy is consumed internally; no new public request or SQL binding is claimed by this scope.

Physical directory identity is normalized resolved-path identity. Hard-linked files intentionally retain separate path candidates, as required by the scope contract.
The link policy remains an internal implementation seam until the later request binder exposes explicit scope options; no public API is claimed here.
